No causal attribution of the later speed reduction to wind is made.
Mobile and SpeedCoach distances are not averaged because the mobile distance is flagged biased.

claims.statement: SpeedCoach and mobile recordings describe the same outing, supported by route overlap; their starts differ by 37 seconds.

limitations: This establishes rate compliance only; telemetry does not verify resistance-band use.
claims.statement: Reconstructed work intervals 1–3 averaged 20.02, 20.02, and 19.97 SPM, within the planned 19–21 SPM range.
Work intervals 4 and 6 averaged 22.99 and 22.97 SPM, within the planned 22–24 SPM range.

limitations: The timing supports an association only, not wind as the cause of the speed change or any conclusion about athlete regression.
claims.statement: Average reconstructed speed declined from 3.459 m/s in work-04 to 2.970 m/s in work-05 while effective headwind had changed from the initial -1.0 m/s tailwind to +5.5 m/s headwind; work-06 averaged 3.168 m/s under the continued headwind.
Resistance-band use for the first three intervals, and removal before the final three, cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence.

limitations: No coach observation or perceived-effort report is supplied; GPS and stroke rate cannot establish these attributes.
claims.statement: Technique, crew synchronization, and perceived effort are not established.

coach_briefing: Six work intervals and five active recoveries were reconstructed. Rate execution was on target for work 1–4 and 6; work-05 was the clear deviation at 19.99 SPM versus the planned 22–24. Speed fell from 3.459 m/s in work-04 to 2.970 m/s in work-05 as effective headwind shifted to +5.5 m/s, then was 3.168 m/s in work-06; this is an association, not a causal finding. Confirm band use and the reason for the fifth-repetition rate drop.

deviations.description: Work-05 averaged 19.99 SPM, approximately 2.01 SPM below the planned 22–24 SPM range for the final three repetitions.

limitations: Weather timing cannot establish athlete improvement, regression, or the cause of a performance change.
environment_assessment.summary: Effective headwind changed from -1.0 m/s at the start (tailwind by this convention) to +5.5 m/s, crossing sign at 1,800 s during work-04 and remaining +5.5 m/s through work-06. This temporal change is associated with the observed later-work speed change but does not establish causation.

follow_up_questions: Was the resistance band used for work intervals 1–3 and removed before work interval 4?
Why did work-05 remain near 20 SPM rather than the planned 22–24 SPM?
Was there any interruption, maneuver, safety issue, or crew decision during work-05?
What was the crew's perceived effort during work intervals 4–6?

prescribed_blocks: 3 × 1,000 m at 19–21 SPM with resistance band; 180–300 s active recovery
3 × 1,000 m at 22–24 SPM without resistance band; 180–300 s active recovery
plan_summary.summary: Plan: 6 × 1 km, first three work intervals at 19–21 SPM with a resistance band, last three at 22–24 SPM without it, with 180–300 s active recoveries. Reconstructed telemetry identifies six work intervals and five recoveries; the fifth work interval is below its prescribed stroke-rate range.

session_associations.reason: The recordings are assessed as the same outing from bidirectional GPS-route overlap despite a preserved 37-second start-clock offset.

source_policy.reason: SpeedCoach reports SPM; mobile SPM is flagged all-zero and rejected.
SpeedCoach is selected because mobile cumulative distance is flagged biased; the sources differ by 1.2%, so values were not averaged.
SpeedCoach provides the time-window speed used for work-interval comparison; mobile supplies no corresponding time-window telemetry in this summary.
SpeedCoach route is selected and mobile GPS corroborates route overlap; clock disagreement remains unresolved.
Environment is a separate synthetic high-quality timeline, time-aligned to SpeedCoach; it is not interchangeable with onboard telemetry.
